note: Frozen debt: edges ADR-0007's matrix forbids and the tree still has. Shrink it; do not grow it. Seven clusters, and they are not equally hard. (1) `libs/delivery/*` reaching for infrastructure is eight of the twenty-four, and `delivery-host` is five of those: it is called host because it IS a shell -- the bus, a Postgres reader, both observability packages and service-bootstrap, the whole of it wired in one file -- wearing a domain badge. P9J7X puts vendors behind the `libs/delivery` port and will move some of this; the host's own infrastructure edges want a card of their own, and the honest question that card answers is whether `delivery/host` belongs in `libs/` at all rather than beside the units it boots. (2) `@polaris/governance -> @polaris/observability-logger` is one import in one file (`src/metrics.ts`) and is the cheapest entry here to clear -- a domain library that emits its own telemetry is the textbook case for taking the emitter as an argument. (3) The two `libs/archive` edges are smaller than the card that filed them assumed. `archive-writer -> bus` is a TYPE-ONLY import of `Checkpoint` and `CheckpointStore`; `archive-replay -> runtime-environments` is replay's only forbidden edge, and replay does not import the bus at all. The 'replay re-emits onto streams, so give it a port' follow-up has no code under it today: whatever re-emits lives outside this library. (4) `@polaris/spec -> @polaris/runtime-environments` is the last of the kernel's three edges and the only one that was ever debt. WNGW6 took the other two to the architect and ADR-0007's 2026-08-21 amendment settled them: the law is 'the kernel imports no POLARIS package', so `zod` and `yaml` are the notation a schema kernel expresses schemas in, and they left this file for the KERNEL_THIRD_PARTY allow-list in `lint-import-direction.mjs` with the reason recorded at each entry. What remains is the law's actual subject -- `envelope/primitives.ts` imports `polarisEnvironmentSchema`, so the kernel cannot be built without a package that parses the process environment. It clears when the environment vocabulary moves down into spec, or when the envelope stops naming it. (5) `polaris-cli` imports four `async/` processors to register and emit their work. The CLI wants the registration and emitter logic, not the runnable; those belong in `libs/engage` (Q7COB) and `libs/warehouse`, and this cluster is the clearest evidence for those carve-outs. (6) `sync-enrichment-runtime-v1` imports its geoip and traits siblings, which is one unit composing two others -- the shape 'nothing imports a unit' exists to name. It clears when the enrichment physics moves into a library and the three units stop being a hierarchy. (7) The six `libs/tenancy` edges arrived WITH their classification rather than before it: the same amendment made tenancy domain, and six edges that had been legal by omission became debt on the day the matrix learned to look at them. Two shapes, and only one of them is expensive. `tenancy-project-config -> persistence-postgres` and `-> observability-logger` are TYPE-ONLY (`Database`, `Logger`), as is most of `-> runtime-environments`; the store already takes its Kysely handle and its logger as constructor options, so what is left is vocabulary, and it clears when those types are declared where the meaning is instead of borrowed from the driver. The value imports are the real ones: `project-config/destination-lookup.ts` calls `isPolarisEnvironment`, `control-plane/gate.ts` re-exports `POLARIS_ENVIRONMENTS` as `GATE_ENVIRONMENTS`, and `control-plane/resolver.ts` defaults to `runtime-secrets`' `verifySecret`. `persistence-control-plane -> tenancy-control-plane` is the mirror and the sharpest of the seven: the Postgres mutation layer imports `assertNoMappingSemantics` and `maskIfSecret`, which is a driver enforcing meaning rather than storing it. Compose the two in a unit, or lift the mutation rules above the driver.
